# Behavioral Specification: SPI Device RX FIFO Control Module

## 1. Overview

This module transfers a byte stream from a byte-source FIFO into a circular receive buffer in SRAM. It packs received bytes into SRAM-width words before writing them to memory. It performs full-word writes when enough bytes have been gathered, and masked partial-word writes when a programmable wait timer expires with only partial data available.

The module is responsible only for the receive data path from the byte FIFO into the SRAM circular buffer. It does not parse commands or addresses, and it never reads from the SRAM.

## 2. Reset and Configuration

On reset, the module shall:

- enter an idle state with no pending SRAM write;
- clear any partially assembled word state;
- set the write pointer to offset zero within the configured region;
- deassert the write request;
- present a fill level consistent with the externally supplied read pointer.

The module shall use the configured start and end addresses to define the circular buffer region. The end address is the last valid memory word of the region. The module shall not generate an SRAM write address outside this region.

The read pointer is an input and is never modified by the module. The write pointer is maintained and exposed by the module.

## 3. Byte Reception and Packing

While no SRAM write is pending and the buffer is not full, the module shall accept bytes from the byte-source FIFO using a valid/ready handshake. The module shall accept at most one byte per cycle and shall not assert ready unless it can consume the byte without loss.

Accepted bytes shall be placed into the current memory word in arrival order:

- the first byte for a word goes into byte lane 0;
- the second byte goes into byte lane 1;
- the process continues until all byte lanes of the memory word have been filled.

The module shall not accept more bytes once the current word is full until the full-word write has been performed.

If the byte source is empty and no partial word is pending, the module shall remain idle and shall not perform any write.

## 4. Partial Data and Wait Timer

If the byte source becomes empty while the current word is only partially filled, the module shall start a wait period based on the configured timer value.

During the wait period:

- If a new byte arrives before the timer expires, the module shall accept the byte and continue filling the current word.
- If the word remains partial and the byte source becomes empty again, the wait period shall restart.
- If no byte arrives before the timer expires, the module shall perform a masked partial-word write of the accumulated bytes.
- If a byte arrives on the exact cycle the timer expires, the byte shall take priority and the partial write shall be postponed.

A timer value of zero shall cause the partial-word write to be initiated as soon as the byte source is empty and the current word is partial.

## 5. SRAM Write Behavior

The module shall perform writes only; it shall never issue an SRAM read request.

When a write is required, the module shall:

- present the address of the current memory word within the configured buffer region;
- present the accumulated write data for that word;
- present a write mask selecting the byte lanes that contain valid accumulated data;
- assert the write request and hold it until the memory indicates acceptance.

For a full-word write, the mask shall cover all byte lanes.

For a partial-word write, the mask shall cover all byte lanes that have been loaded for the current word. Byte lanes not covered by the mask must remain unchanged in memory.

The module shall not start another write or accept more byte-FIFO data while a write request is pending.

The module shall ignore any read-data return and any read-error indication from the memory, since it never performs reads.

## 6. Write Pointer and Wrap Behavior

The write pointer shall be updated only after an SRAM write has been accepted. Until then, the write pointer and fill level shall not advance.

### Full-word write

When a full word has been written:

- if the word is the last word of the configured region, the write pointer shall wrap to the start of the region and its wrap indicator shall toggle;
- otherwise, the write pointer shall advance to the next word and clear its byte offset.

### Partial-word write

A partial-word write shall not complete the current word. The byte-lane accumulation state shall be retained so that later bytes can continue filling the same word.

After a partial-word write, the write pointer shall remain at the same word address and shall advance only to the byte offset following the last accumulated byte. The region wrap shall not occur on a partial write, even if the partial write is to the last word of the region.

When the remaining byte lanes of that word are eventually filled, the module shall perform a full-word write and then advance the pointer according to the full-word rules.

## 7. Full Status and Fill Level

The module shall expose a full-status indication and a fill-level value.

The full status shall indicate whether the circular buffer has space to accept a new full memory word. It shall be based on the relationship between the read pointer and the write pointer, including the wrap indicator. It shall not block completion of a word that is already partially accumulated.

The fill level shall be the current number of valid bytes in the circular buffer, computed from the read pointer and the write pointer. It shall be zero when the buffer is empty and equal to the region size in bytes when the buffer is full. Bytes that have been accepted from the byte FIFO but not yet committed to SRAM shall not be included in the fill level until the corresponding SRAM write has been accepted.

# Behavioral Specification: SPI Device Firmware Mode Module

## 1. Purpose

The module implements the SPI firmware mode data path. It transfers raw data between the SPI interface and internal SRAM buffer regions, without parsing commands or addresses. It operates as a byte-oriented, full-duplex streaming bridge:

- Bytes received from the SPI input side are buffered and written into the receive SRAM region.
- Bytes stored in the transmit SRAM region are read out and delivered to the SPI output side.
- Receive and transmit operations can occur concurrently.

The module is intended for bulk data movement, such as downloading or uploading firmware images, and does not implement SPI flash opcodes, memory-mapped addressing, or higher-level protocols.

## 2. Clocking and Reset Behavior

The module spans multiple clock domains:

- The receive byte interface is associated with the SPI receive clock.
- The transmit byte interface is associated with the SPI output clock.
- The SRAM interface, circular buffer pointers, and SRAM-side control logic are associated with the main system clock.

The module shall preserve data in the asynchronous FIFOs when the associated SPI clock is stopped. SRAM-side draining and prefetching shall continue whenever the main system clock is running, independent of whether the SPI clocks are active.

The receive and transmit FIFO paths shall have independent reset controls. Asserting the reset for one FIFO path shall discard its contents, clear its status flags, and reset its depth to zero. It shall not affect the other FIFO path.

Resetting the main system side shall clear all SRAM-side control state, pointer outputs, and in-progress SRAM operations.

Configuration inputs, including buffer base and limit indices and the receive partial-write timer value, must be stable while the SPI interface is operating. The module does not synchronize changes to these configuration values during operation.

## 3. Receive Data Path

The module shall accept incoming byte data from the SPI receive side whenever a byte is presented.

Each received byte shall be stored in the receive FIFO if space is available.

The receive interface shall not provide backpressure to the upstream byte source. Therefore, if a byte is presented while the receive FIFO is full, the module shall discard that byte and assert the receive overflow indication. The overflow indication shall be asserted for that attempted write condition.

The receive FIFO shall provide:

- An empty indication, visible to the SRAM-side read logic, when no received bytes are waiting to be drained.
- A full indication, visible to the SPI-side write logic, when no further bytes can be accepted.
- A fill-depth indication so the rest of the system can observe how much data is buffered.

The module shall not drop received bytes except when the receive FIFO is full.

## 4. Transmit Data Path

The module shall provide a byte stream to the SPI output side.

The module shall present a byte whenever the SPI output side is ready to receive one. This byte-present indication shall be asserted unconditionally, regardless of whether the transmit FIFO contains valid data.

If the transmit FIFO is not empty, the byte presented shall be the next stored byte. Consuming that byte shall advance the transmit FIFO.

If the transmit FIFO is empty, the byte value presented is not meaningful. The module shall assert the transmit underflow indication when the SPI side consumes a byte while the FIFO is empty.

The transmit FIFO shall provide:

- An empty indication, visible to the SPI output side, when no data is available to transmit.
- A full indication, visible to the SRAM-side control logic, when no more data can be written into the FIFO.
- A fill-depth indication.

## 5. SRAM Circular Buffer Management

The module shall manage two circular SRAM regions: one for received data and one for transmitted data.

Each region is defined by a base index and a limit index. The module shall confine its SRAM accesses to the configured regions and shall not access addresses outside them.

### 5.1 Receive Region

Received bytes drained from the receive FIFO shall be written into the receive SRAM region.

The module shall maintain the receive write pointer and expose it externally. The software shall provide the receive read pointer, which indicates how much space has been freed by software.

The module shall indicate when the receive SRAM region is full. When full, the module shall stop draining the receive FIFO into SRAM. This will cause the receive FIFO to fill, and subsequent incoming bytes will be dropped with overflow asserted.

The module may accumulate received bytes into full SRAM-word quantities before writing. If fewer than a full word remains pending and the configured timer expires, the module shall perform a partial-word write. For such partial writes, the write strobes shall be asserted only for the byte lanes containing valid received data.

### 5.2 Transmit Region

Data to be transmitted shall be read from the transmit SRAM region and written into the transmit FIFO whenever:

- The transmit SRAM region contains unread data, and
- The transmit FIFO has space available.

The module shall maintain the transmit read pointer and expose it externally. The software shall provide the transmit write pointer, which indicates how much data has been made available by software.

The transmit read pointer shall advance as data is read from SRAM and loaded into the transmit FIFO.

The module shall sample the transmit write pointer for the purpose of a fill operation. Changes to the write pointer while a fill operation is in progress shall take effect on a subsequent fill operation.

### 5.3 Abort Behavior

When the abort request is asserted, the module shall stop the transmit SRAM-to-FIFO fill operation. It shall not issue further transmit SRAM reads while abort is asserted.

Aborting the transmit fill path shall not affect the receive data path or the contents of the FIFOs.

When abort is deasserted, the transmit fill path shall resume using the then-current transmit write pointer.

## 6. SRAM Port Sharing

The receive and transmit paths share a single SRAM master interface. The module shall serialize their access requests so that both paths can make progress.

The SRAM interface shall present the address, write enable, write data, and write strobes for each access. Read data returned from SRAM shall be consumed by the transmit path and stored into the transmit FIFO.

The module shall avoid deadlock when both receive and transmit paths require SRAM access at the same time.

## 7. Status and Error Indication

The module shall expose the following status information:

- Receive FIFO empty, full, and depth.
- Transmit FIFO empty, full, and depth.
- Receive SRAM region depth and full status.
- Transmit SRAM region depth.

The empty and full flags for each FIFO correspond to different clock domains. The empty flag is meaningful on the side that consumes data from the FIFO, while the full flag is meaningful on the side that writes data into the FIFO.

The module shall expose two error indications:

- Receive overflow: asserted when a received byte is presented while the receive FIFO is full.
- Transmit underflow: asserted when the SPI output side consumes a byte while the transmit FIFO is empty.

These error indications are generated in the SPI clock domains and reflect the raw condition at the time it occurs.

## 8. Data Integrity and Protocol Behavior

The module shall treat all received bytes as data. It shall not modify, parse, or interpret byte values.

The module shall send all transmit bytes exactly as they were stored in the transmit SRAM region.

The module shall always select single-bit SPI I/O mode. It shall not switch to dual or quad SPI operation.

The module is not responsible for bit-level serialization or deserialization. It operates on complete bytes.
